findings.reason: §1b must state how first_circuit is supplied and how the wall's non-limiter contours survive the migration, or it silently loses the wall contour §2 promises.
findings.text: §1's reuse note calls the four struct-level readers "pure functions of the raw IDS structs with no adapter transform", but read_artifact_pf_passive takes a required positional first_circuit and a drives sequence, and read_artifact_limiter (line 671) returns only the first limiter unit, dropping the vessel/plate contours §2 draws as the vessel outline; §1b's plan to move the geometry reader onto these readers rests on that characterisation

findings.reason: those scripts are explicitly scoped out and plot_style.py is genuinely the first shared style module, so the design decision holds even though the reuse note understates what it leaves behind.
findings.text: §1 says the repository's hand-rolled palettes are "the two ... in scripts/figures/wm_demonstration_figs.py and playable_plasma_figs.py", but twelve scripts under scripts/ (bench_matrix_figures.py, figures_topology_census.py, figures_engine_crossval_rca.py, plot_patch_gate_figures.py, plot_current_recovery_findings.py, efcc_greens_columns.py, and others) each define their own colour map, so the survey undercounts the palette surface sixfold

findings.reason: the plan should keep the drawing reader or extend the owner's readers and say why, rather than wrap readers whose interface it must first route through first_circuit and drives to use at all.
findings.text: §1b retires the landed shape dispatch (_shape_from_geometry/_shapes_from_elements, geometry_type-aware: rectangle, annulus, thick_line, oblique, outline) for artifact_geometry readers that exist to source turns, circuits and drives for the forward operator and return PolygonSection vertices, so the script becomes a thin adapter whose interface discards the declared geometry_type the figure draws, and §1b gives no reason the landed reader cannot be kept or the artifact_geometry readers extended to carry the drawn shape

findings.reason: add a read_channel to imas_ambix/data/eddb.py beside write_channel so the cache keeps one owner that both the writer and the figure call, rather than re-deriving the read layout in a script.
findings.text: §3 reads each cached channel (opening the zarr array, its channel_time_path sibling and the UNIT_ATTR unit) inside scripts/figures_jt60sa_signals.py, but imas_ambix/data/eddb.py owns the cache: it builds channel_path/channel_time_path and writes with write_channel, and has no read counterpart, so the addressing is shared while the read is forked into the figure script

duplicate_owner-1.reason: plan v20 §3 adds read_channel to imas_ambix/data/eddb.py beside write_channel, returning a ChannelRecord, with a round-trip test, and the signals script calls it

reuse_search-1.reason: plan v20 §1b passes first_circuit=0 and asserts exactly one wall unit per phase (the store has one limiter unit and no vessel units), failing rather than dropping a contour

reuse_search-2.reason: plan v20 §1 corrects the count to about a dozen scripts with their own colour maps, still scoped out

thin_wrapper-1.reason: the v10 review's duplicate_owner finding asked for exactly this migration; read_artifact_* return PolygonSection vertices, which are the drawn shape for every element in this store (all rectangles), so keeping a parallel geometry_type dispatch would restore the duplicate, and extending the owner's readers is not needed for any shape the store carries

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — imas_ambix/plot_style.py hides the sheet vendoring, the role contract and the label helper behind four names; the geometry script hides catalogue addressing and the IDS reads behind read_phase and cross_section.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — §3 reads the EDDB cache inside scripts/figures_jt60sa_signals.py while imas_ambix/data/eddb.py owns the cache and has no read counterpart to its own write_channel.
rubric_items.interface_budget: pass — public_definitions 0, cli_options 0, mcp_views 0, refusal_families 0; every section names what it retires or states why nothing can be: §1b retires the reader's own root-and-name join and shape dispatch, §1 states the style module is the first and retires nothing (imas_ambix/ holds no plotting style code), §3 states its script is the first to draw a JT-60SA signal and retires nothing.
rubric_items.reuse_search: a finding — the search cites the geometry readers as pure IDS-struct functions, but imas_ambix/gs/artifact_geometry.py:409 needs a required first_circuit, and it counts two inline palettes where twelve scripts carry their own.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: a finding — §1b retires the landed geometry_type-aware shape dispatch for artifact_geometry readers built for the forward operator, without justifying why the landed reader cannot be kept or the readers extended.
